cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
description: The admin changelist for User lists the 'password' column for every user. If the app's custom User model stores plaintext or weakly hashed passwords, anyone with admin view access, or anyone who can see an admin screen, can read all credentials. Admin-site XSS or shoulder-surfing would expose them as well.

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
description: The DELETE statement is built by string-formatting blabberUsername and self.username directly into the SQL. An attacker who controls either value can inject SQL and alter or delete arbitrary rows.

cwe_name: Missing Password Field Masking
description: The password and cpassword fields are plain CharFields with no PasswordInput widget. They render as visible text inputs, which exposes the typed password to shoulder surfing and can leave it in browser autofill or history.

cwe_name: Missing Password Field Masking
description: The ModelForm exposes the model's 'password' field without overriding its widget, so it renders as a visible text input instead of a masked password field.

cwe_name: Use of Weak Credentials
description: A new user's initial password is set to their own username, and the password hint is also the username, so anyone who knows a username can guess the password and log in.

cwe_name: Use of Weak Hash
description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is fast and easy to crack with rainbow tables or brute force if the database is exposed.

cwe_name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
description: The TOTP secret is stored in plaintext in the database, so a database leak lets an attacker generate valid second-factor codes. The password hint is also stored in plaintext.

cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
description: The user-supplied blabid is appended to the redirect URL without validation. Because it follows a relative path, exploitation is limited, but unvalidated input still controls the redirect target (including query injection and CRLF-style manipulation).

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
description: The 'sort' GET parameter is concatenated directly into the ORDER BY clause, and the username is also interpolated. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL.

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
description: The user-supplied POST parameter 'command' is transformed and passed to eval(), allowing arbitrary Python code execution on the server.

cwe_name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: The state-changing POST handler (listen/ignore actions) is decorated with csrf_exempt, disabling CSRF protection.

cwe_name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: The attacker-controlled HTTP Host header is used to build a URL that the server requests with urllib.request.urlopen. An attacker can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts (blind SSRF), for example by sending a crafted Host header.
vulnerable_snippet:
host_ip = request.META['HTTP_HOST'].split(':')[0]
            print("da")
            redir = urllib.request.Request('http://' + host_ip + ':' + request.META['SERVER_PORT'] + '/feed')
            urllib.request.urlopen(redir, timeout=5)

cwe_name: Improper Certificate Validation
description: The httplib2 client is created with disable_ssl_certificate_validation=True, so TLS certificates are not verified. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound requests.

cwe_name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: Credentials are hard-coded in the source and passed to the HTTP client. Anyone with access to the code can recover them.

cwe_name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: A destructive, state-changing database flush runs on a POST with only a 'confirm' parameter. There is no authentication, authorization or CSRF token check in the code shown, so any visitor or a cross-site request can wipe the database.

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
description: SQL statements are built by string formatting with '%' on user attributes and executed. The values come from hard-coded data, so it is not currently exploitable, but the pattern is unsafe.
vulnerable_snippet:
cursor.execute(usersStatement % (user.username, user.password, user.password_hint, user.totp_secret, user.created_at,
                                                     user.last_login, user.real_name, user.blab_name))

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
description: The user-controlled POST parameter 'fortunefile' is interpolated into a shell command passed to os.system without sanitization. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf /`) to execute arbitrary commands, or read arbitrary files.

cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
description: The user-supplied 'host' value is passed as a positional argument to ping with no validation. Although no shell is used, a value beginning with '-' can be interpreted as an option by ping, enabling argument injection.

cwe_name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
description: The 'user' cookie is attacker-controlled. It is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads, which allows arbitrary code execution through a crafted pickle payload.
